data.title: Battle rez in one click: a dead list anyone can call from
data.text:
Mythic+ leader: "Someone dies mid-pull and I don't have time to click their corpse, then the rez button, then check who is alive."
When a groupmate dies their name shows in a small strip; one click (or a keybind or macro) picks the best living rezzer and calls it. In a 5-player group anyone may call, it goes to instance chat in Group Finder groups, and it can whisper the rezzer. With several dead, the leader's order (healers, tanks, damage) decides who is first.

Today: target the dead player, then /cdc rez or the Rez button; leader or assist only; party or raid chat

data.title: Post what's ready to raid chat
data.text:
Raid leader: "I want one click that tells the raid which defensives are up, so my healers stop asking in chat."
A button and a slash command that post one short line to raid or officer chat: what's ready and who has it, and what's back when. You pick which spells go in the line.
tags: Partly on Retail and Forever: only players who run it
Today: only Request Rez posts to chat

data.title: Rotation order for a cooldown
data.text:
Raid leader: "I rotate Hand of Sacrifice and Guardian Spirit through the same few people, and I want the list to show who is next."
The leader sets an order for a spell (Kyle, then Ann, then Joe). The panel marks the next ready player in line and moves on when it's used; the order can be shared with the group.
tags: Partly on Retail and Forever: only players who run it
Today: no order; Request Rez takes the first ready provider

data.title: Rezzers to skip
data.text:
Raid leader: "I never want my main healer's Rebirth or Soulstone called unless there is no one else."

data.title: Guild-wide cooldown view
data.text:
Guild master: "My officers want to see what the other raid team has ready without joining their group."
An optional guild mode, off by default, that also shares cooldowns over the guild channel, with a small list of who in the guild runs it and what they have ready.
tags: Partly: only guild members who run it, on every client
Today: messages go only to the group (party, raid or instance)

data.title: Officers can send a setup to the guild
data.text:
Guild master: "When we change our raid plan I want to send the new spell list to everyone once."
An officer sends a spell list and a few options over the guild channel; each member gets Accept, Not now or Never from this person, and can undo it.
tags: Possible on every client (members who run it)
Today: each player sets spells by hand

data.title: Show only my raid team
data.text:
Guild master: "I run three raid teams and an M+ crowd, and I only care about the team on the pull right now."

data.title: Mark guessed cooldowns on players without the addon
data.text:
Mythic+ leader: "I need to know whether that Shaman really has lust up or whether the addon is just assuming it."
A player who doesn't run the addon and hasn't been seen casting gets a small question mark: "ready as far as we know". Confirmed rows (players who run it, your own readable spells) look normal.
tags: Retail and Forever (Era, TBC and MoP see casts in the combat log)
Today: an unseen provider always shows ready (Roster.lua: no cast seen counts as 0 s left)

data.title: Clear the board when a key starts
data.text:
Mythic+ leader: "Cooldowns reset when the key starts, and I don't want last dungeon's timers telling me lust is on cooldown."
When a key starts (and on entering a new dungeon) tracked cooldowns that the game resets go back to ready and players who left are dropped. One setting turns it off.
tags: Retail for the key start; dungeon entry on every client
Today: nothing reacts to a key start or a zone change

data.text:
Classic raider: "I need to see who is carrying a soulstone before the pull, not find out when the tank wipes us."

data.title: World buffs and more consumables
data.text:
Classic raider: "Half the raid dropped Songflower and Zandalar before the pull and nobody noticed until Onyxia."
Strips like flask and food for world buffs (Dragonslayer, Zandalar, Songflower, Warchief's Blessing, Dire Maul) and for protection potions, elixirs and other consumables, with who lacks them. You choose which show.

data.title: Every way to bring someone back, in one row
data.text:
Classic raider: "When someone dies I want to see in one line who can bring them back: druid, soulstoned, or shaman Ankh."
One Resurrection row adding up ready Rebirths, placed Soulstones and Reincarnations, with the next to come back and a call button.

Today: Rebirth counts as a battle rez; Soulstone is tracked but never listed as a rez
